newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS - Unicom, Sonat natural gas venture.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Unicom, Sonat natural gas venture.

text.p: Unicom Corp. and Sonat Inc. Wednesday formed a joint venture to market natural gas to the $6 billion a year Midwest commercial and industrial market.

The formation of Unicom Gas Services is especially key to Unicom, parent of Chicago-based electric company Commonwealth Edison, as it prepares to defend its turf when the electric market becomes deregulated.

"It is the first signal that they are making an aggressive move to prepare themselves for the deregulation of the electric industry," Catharina Milostan, an analyst who follows the industry for Mesirow Financial, said.

The joint venture was formed by Unicom Energy Services, the unregulated energy marketing subsidiary of Unicom Corp. and Sonat Marketing, the natural gas marketing subsidiary of Birmingham, Ala.-based Sonat Inc.

The up front financial committment for the venture is not significant, as it will use Sonat's existing pipelines and Unicom's marketing resources, William Downey, president of Unicom Energy Services, said.
The companies have an initial commitment of three years for the venture.
That time frame will allow the companies to get a good sense of how much the venture will contribute to earnings and also allows time for deregulation in other states, Milostan said.

Robert Gilpin, who heads the new venture, said the company was aiming to capture 10 percent to 15 percent of the market, which he put at between $6 billion to $8 billion a year, depending on pricing. The market also consists of 8.0 billion cubic feet of natural gas a day, he said.

With this venture and a previous alliance with AliiedSignal Inc to sell small power generators, Unicom is gearing up to provide services to customers who will expect one-stop shopping in a deregulated environment, Downey said.

"Right now, Commonwealth Edison serves customers that have no choice," Downey said. "If they have a choice on what basis will the select Unicom? We're putting in place those key building blocks that we think will define why we are the preeminent supplier."
Unicom had considered other options for entering the commercial and industrial natural gas market, Downey said.
"We looked very hard at all the options and quite frankly, we thought this was an efficient and expedient way to get into this market for our customers," Downey said.
Unicom shares closed up 37.5 cents at $23.125 Wednesday and Sonat closed down 37.5 at $49.50, both on the New York Stock Exchange.
